correctness.rationale: Affine reduce to the standard tetrahedron with x1<=1-s and x2<=1-t. For s,t>=0, s+t<=1, c=s^3+t^3<1, the disjoint cap-volume calculation is vol=(1-c)/6. The coordinate facets have areas (1-t^2)/2, (1-s^2)/2 and (1-s^2-t^2)/2. By the mixed-area formula with support h_{-K}, the other outward facets have zero support and 6V(K,K,-K) equals their weighted sum N. Independent symbolic expansion verifies rho-5/3=(1-u)((1-u)(5u+4)+12st)/[3(1-c)], u=s+t, so equality requires u=1. Fixing c, st=(u^3-c)/(3u), u ranges c^(1/3)..min((4c)^(1/3),1); differentiation gives dN/du<=u^2-1<0 for 0<u<1, strict also at u=1 when c<1. Endpoints then give one-cap maximum, balanced minimum for c<=1/4, edge-contact minimum thereafter and the explicit quadratic discriminant solutions. The universal proof uses geometry/algebra; finite exact difference-body checks are supplementary.
